transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mr. Hassan, thank you for coming in to see me. I need to talk to you about a mistake we made with your daughter's medication this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Oh. Here we go again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We gave her a dose of medication that was too high. The error happened because instead of weighing her on the scale, we estimated her weight to calculate the dose. This meant she received a significant amount more than the safe limit for a child her size.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Right.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Does that make sense so far, or can I explain that part differently?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I get it. You guessed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I did. I was the one who made that calculation, and I am very sorry. I take full responsibility for this error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's always something.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Does the fact that the dose was above the safety threshold make sense to you, or do you have a question about what that means for her?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I've heard it all before. Just tell me if she's dying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. It's frustrating. Let's get into exactly what we are doing now to manage this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Sure.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: First, we have already started a continuous heart rate and blood pressure monitor. We are checking her vitals every fifteen minutes for the next four hours. I have also consulted the toxicology team, and they have confirmed that we need to keep her on a saline drip for the next twelve hours to help her kidneys clear the medication.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm also scheduling a follow-up blood test for 2:00 PM today to check her drug levels. I want you to watch for any unusual drowsiness or rash, and if you see anything, press the call button immediately.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: To make sure this doesn't happen again, I've already flagged this with the nursing lead. From now on, no medication will be drawn for your daughter unless there is a fresh weight recorded on the chart from the actual scale within the last twenty-four hours.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Whatever.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is exhausting for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You have no idea.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're tired of this. But look, I actually have to go check on another patient's labs right now, so let's wrap this up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't ask for anything anyway.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. So, to recap: vitals every fifteen minutes, bloods at 2:00 PM, and you notify us of any drowsiness. I will be back in thirty minutes to check her again.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Thank you for your time. I'll be back soon.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language at the end of the encounter ('let's wrap this up' because they 'have to go check on another patient').

E.justification: Error named in first turn, lay language used, comprehension checked twice ('Does that make sense so far', 'make sense to you'), and no false reassurance given.

A.justification: Direct apology used ('I am very sorry'), resident takes full personal responsibility, and maintains this accountability despite patient pushback.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating', 'exhausting', 'tired') and engages with the patient's emotional bids.

T.justification: Plan includes specific steps with timelines (vitals every 15 mins, bloods at 2 PM), a named patient role (watch for drowsiness/rash), and a prevention strategy (fresh weight requirement).
